paras: The southern blue jewel-babbler (Ptilorrhoa nigricrissus) is a species of bird in the family Cinclosomatidae, endemic to the southern lowlands of New Guinea. It was described by Tommaso Salvadori in 1876. It is monotypic.
This species was formerly considered conspecific with the blue jewel-babbler, but was split from it based on morphological differences, ecology and the call.
This species is similar to the blue jewel-babbler, but the female has a small white stripe above the eye, the undertail is black, and the undertail coverts are partly marked with black.
This species lacks the characteristic hezok call of the blue jewel-babbler.

This species is found in the southern lowlands of New Guinea in both Indonesian Western New Guinea and Papua New Guinea. It is found from the Wanggar River and Etna Bay to the Milne Bay. In the Bird's Neck Isthmus, its range overlaps with the blue jewel-babbler, however, it separates altitudinally, with this species occupying a higher elevation.
